utokyo-global-unit-courses-2027.about:
UTokyo Global Unit Courses (GUC) are short, intensive, English-taught courses at the University of Tokyo, organised in two-week terms across June and July. Students can take in-person or online courses and earn Global Unit Certificates.

GUC is open to full-time undergraduate and graduate students at non-Japanese universities who have completed at least one term, with TOEFL iBT 90 / IELTS 6.5. Partner-network (AUA, IARU, USTEP) students may get 20% off.

Details for GUC 2027 will be posted around the second week of January 2027. For reference, 2026 fees were JPY 190,000 per in-person 1-unit course and JPY 40,000 per online half-unit course, with applications from early February to mid-March.
highlights: Japan's top university
In-person or online options
20% discount for AUA/IARU/USTEP students
utokyo-global-unit-courses-2027.eligibility: Full-time undergraduate or graduate students at non-Japanese universities, at least one completed term; TOEFL iBT 90 / IELTS 6.5.
how_to_apply: Watch the GUC page for 2027 details (around mid-January 2027).
Register on the UTokyo application system (TAO).
Submit transcript, student ID and English score and pay the JPY 5,000 fee.
Pay course fees after selection; arrange your own housing.
utokyo-global-unit-courses-2027.costs: 2027 fees TBA (2026: JPY 190,000 per in-person 1-unit course, JPY 380,000 for 2-unit, JPY 40,000 online 0.5-unit; JPY 5,000 application fee). No campus housing. FUTI scholarship for US students.

uva-online-winter-courses-2027.about:
Every January the University of Amsterdam offers short online winter courses taught in English by UvA academics, open to students and professionals worldwide. For January 2027 the courses include Introduction to AI Ethics and Decision-Making and Existential Psychology for Contemporary Life (both online, 18–29 January 2027), Introduction to Western Esotericism, and a three-week online course, Birding Across Borders.

Courses are intensive and some include a preparatory assignment. Students from UNICA, Universitas 21 or LERU universities can request a EUR 100 partial scholarship on eligible courses (first-come, first-served), and UvA summer/winter alumni get EUR 75 off.
highlights: Learn from UvA academics without travelling
Two-week intensive online format in January
Small partial scholarships for network universities
uva-online-winter-courses-2027.eligibility: Mostly university students and professionals; each course states its own entry requirements. All nationalities; online.
how_to_apply: Choose a 2027 winter course on the UvA Summer School site
Apply online with a motivation letter by 13 December 2026
Indicate an eligible scholarship or alumni discount in the form if applicable
Pay the tuition after admission and complete any preparatory assignment
uva-online-winter-courses-2027.costs: Two-week online courses: EUR 925 regular tuition (EUR 875 early bird, passed). Scholarships: UNICA/U21/LERU partial EUR 100; alumni discount EUR 75.

viu-scicomm-spring-school-2027.about:
Venice International University's spring school 'Equipping Researchers with Skills, Strategies and Confidence for Science Communication' (4th edition) runs 8–12 March 2027 on San Servolo island in Venice. It covers strategic research communication, publics and media, informal communication (museums, events, art), evaluation and the impacts of research, through lectures, simulations, case studies and site visits; participants can present their own research.

Faculty come from VIU, Stellenbosch University, LMU Munich, the University of Padua and the University of Bordeaux. Completion earns 2 ECTS.

Open to graduate students and researchers in natural and social sciences, engineering and humanities. Fee €800 (€400 for VIU member universities), including lunches and social events. Apply by 2 November 2026.
highlights: On San Servolo island, Venice
Faculty from five European/African universities
Present your own research
viu-scicomm-spring-school-2027.eligibility: Researchers and graduate (master's/PhD) students in natural and social sciences, engineering and humanities; open to non-member universities.
how_to_apply: Read the programme and brochure.
Complete the online application form by 2 November 2026.
Ask your university about Erasmus+ mobility funding.
Pay the fee after acceptance.
viu-scicomm-spring-school-2027.costs: €800 (other universities) or €400 (VIU members), incl. VAT, tuition, materials, lunches and social events. Travel and accommodation extra. Erasmus+ grants possible for EU PhD/post-docs.

viu-winter-school-digital-rights-2027.about:
Venice International University runs a one-week Winter School on 'Digital Rights: Theory and Practice' on San Servolo island, 25–29 January 2027. VIU schools are aimed at undergraduate, master's, PhD and post-doc students and young academics, and are open to applicants from outside VIU's member universities.

The school examines how fundamental rights apply in the digital sphere, combining theory with practical cases.

The call closes on 1 November 2026; fees and the application form are on the school page.
highlights: One week in Venice
Open to non-member universities
Law and technology focus
viu-winter-school-digital-rights-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate, master's, PhD and post-doc students and young academics; open to applicants outside VIU membership.
how_to_apply: Read the school page.
Submit the online application by 1 November 2026.
Pay the fee after acceptance.
viu-winter-school-digital-rights-2027.costs: Fee on the school page (VIU schools typically include tuition, lunches and social events; travel and accommodation extra).

vlaamse-wiskunde-olympiade-2027.about:
The VWO (upper secondary) and JWO (lower secondary) are Flanders' national maths olympiads, supported by Belgian universities. Round 1 is sat at school; the best go to round 2 and the final, and finalists can enter training for the Benelux, European Girls' and International Mathematical Olympiads.

Results are announced at a proclamation on 19 May 2027.
highlights: Junior (JWO) and senior (VWO) levels
Three rounds, Jan–Apr 2027
Path to BxMO, EGMO and IMO
vlaamse-wiskunde-olympiade-2027.eligibility: Students at secondary schools in Flanders/Belgium (Dutch-language), registered by their school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's VWO coordinator to register you by 23 Nov 2026
Practise with past questions or usolv-it
Sit round 1 on 13 Jan 2027

vub-nova-summer-school-eu-policy-making-.about:
This Jean Monnet Summer School is organised by the Brussels School of Governance (VUB) and NOVA University Lisbon. Week one in Brussels covers the main EU institutions and decision-making procedures; week two at NOVA's Campolide campus in Lisbon covers the EU's role in the world: trade, development, technology, sustainability and relations with other regions.

Study visits to EU institutions, a simulation game on a real policy file and a foresight workshop make it highly practical. It is worth 6 ECTS and counts towards the Postgraduate Certificate in EU Policy Making.

The 2027 edition runs 28 June – 9 July 2027. Applications are open until 26 April 2027, with a 10% early-bird discount before 15 March.
highlights: Two capitals: Brussels and Lisbon
Study visits to EU institutions
10% early-bird discount before 15 March 2027
vub-nova-summer-school-eu-policy-making-.eligibility: Advanced bachelor's and master's students and young professionals interested in EU affairs; any nationality; English.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page and admission criteria.
Apply via the online form.
Apply before 15 March 2027 for the early-bird discount.
Final deadline 26 April 2027; assessment starts February 2027.
vub-nova-summer-school-eu-policy-making-.costs: Tuition on the BSoG Tuition page; 10% early-bird discount. Travel and accommodation not included.

wamunc-xxix-2027.about:
WAMUNC is the George Washington University high-school Model UN, bringing delegates to Foggy Bottom in Washington, D.C., the heart of American policymaking. It is known for its crisis committees.

The conference runs 18–21 March 2027 at Foggy Bottom, Washington, D.C., United States. It is open to high school students and school delegations. Working language: English.

Use the Registration Form on the official site; see 'Registration Information' and 'Financial Information'. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 18–21 March 2027 in Washington, United States
Crisis-heavy conference in Washington, D.C.
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
wamunc-xxix-2027.eligibility: Open to high school students and school delegations. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Use the Registration Form on the official site; see 'Registration Information' and 'Financial Information'.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
wamunc-xxix-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

wharton-ai-leadership-2027.about:
AI Leadership is a selective two-week residential programme on the Wharton campus exploring the impact of artificial intelligence on business and society. Sessions cover the AI landscape, foundations of AI and generative AI, ethical AI and governance, real-world business applications, leadership skills and hands-on workshops with AI tools; students also go on site visits and finish with a team project, receiving a Wharton Global Youth certificate.

The 2027 session runs 20 June–3 July in Philadelphia for students currently in grades 9–11. The 2027 fee is USD 8,599 plus a USD 100 application fee. The programme page does not state international eligibility separately; Wharton Global Youth's other summer programmes welcome international applicants, so international students should confirm with whartonyouth@wharton.upenn.edu before applying.
highlights: Hands-on generative-AI tool workshops
Ethics and governance of AI for business
Two-week format, cheaper than three-week Wharton programmes
wharton-ai-leadership-2027.eligibility: Students currently in grades 9–11. International eligibility is not stated on the programme page; confirm with Wharton Global Youth (other Wharton summer programmes accept international applicants).
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 programme page and check your grade fits
Create an account and submit the Wharton Global Youth online application (opens November 2026)
Upload transcript, short essays and a recommendation as requested; pay the USD 100 application fee
Apply by the priority deadline (27 January 2027) for the best chance of a place and of scholarship review
If admitted, confirm your place and arrange a US visa if you are not American
wharton-ai-leadership-2027.costs: 2027 fee USD 8,599 plus USD 100 application fee; travel and visa extra. Limited scholarships for specific groups only.

wharton-data-science-academy-2027.about:
Data Science Academy is a three-week residential programme at the Wharton School for high-school students who want to learn how data drives decisions in business and society. Students learn statistics and programming for data analysis, work with real datasets, attend talks by Wharton faculty and complete a team project.

The 2027 session runs 13 June–3 July in Philadelphia. Around 75 students currently in grades 10–11 are selected; international applicants are welcome. The 2027 fee is USD 10,999 plus a USD 100 application fee.
highlights: Hands-on coding and statistics with real data
Small cohort of about 75 students
Open to international applicants
wharton-data-science-academy-2027.eligibility: Students currently in grades 10–11 of any nationality, with good maths and English.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 programme page and check your grade fits
Create an account and submit the Wharton Global Youth online application (opens November 2026)
Upload transcript, short essays and a recommendation as requested; pay the USD 100 application fee
Apply by the priority deadline (27 January 2027) for the best chance of a place and of scholarship review
If admitted, confirm your place and arrange a US visa if you are not American
wharton-data-science-academy-2027.costs: 2027 fee USD 10,999 plus USD 100 application fee; travel and visa extra. Limited scholarships for specific groups only.

wharton-essentials-of-finance-2027.about:
Essentials of Finance is a two-week residential programme at the Wharton School that introduces high-school students to how companies, investors and markets work: valuation, personal and corporate finance, investing and the role of financial institutions. Students attend classes by Wharton instructors, take part in team projects and simulations, and visit the Penn campus and Philadelphia.

In 2027 there are three sessions (6–18 June, 20 June–3 July and 25 July–7 August) for students currently in grades 9–11. International applicants are welcome. The 2027 programme fee is USD 8,599 plus a USD 100 application fee; students receive a Wharton Global Youth certificate of completion.
highlights: Wharton instructors and finance simulations
Three session dates to choose from
Open to grades 9–11 from any country
wharton-essentials-of-finance-2027.eligibility: High-school students currently in grades 9–11, of any nationality, with good English. Selection is based on academic record and motivation.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 programme page and check your grade fits
Create an account and submit the Wharton Global Youth online application (opens November 2026)
Upload transcript, short essays and a recommendation as requested; pay the USD 100 application fee
Apply by the priority deadline (27 January 2027) for the best chance of a place and of scholarship review
If admitted, confirm your place and arrange a US visa if you are not American
wharton-essentials-of-finance-2027.costs: 2027 fee USD 8,599 plus USD 100 application fee; travel, visa and spending money extra. Scholarships are limited to specific groups and fee waivers are not available to international applicants.

wharton-financial-decision-making-online.about:
Financial Decision Making is a selective two-week online summer programme from Wharton Global Youth covering personal finance, financial markets, money and banking, wealth building and financial ethics. Each day combines two hours of live lectures with a TA-led recitation and small-group work; students use Excel and complete a group project.

Sessions run 14–25 June (08:00–11:00 EST) and 5–16 July 2027 (13:00–16:00 EST). It is for students currently in grades 9–12 and international students are explicitly welcome. Priority deadline 27 January 2027, then rolling admission.
highlights: Personal finance, markets and banking taught by Wharton
Hands-on Excel and group project
International students welcome
wharton-financial-decision-making-online.eligibility: Students currently in grades 9–12 from any country; no finance background required.
how_to_apply: Check the 2027 session dates and time block on the programme page
Submit the Wharton Global Youth online application (opens November 2026)
Apply by the 27 January 2027 priority deadline (later applications are considered while places remain)
Pay tuition once admitted and test your internet connection and time zone
wharton-financial-decision-making-online.costs: Paid online programme; fees on Wharton Global Youth's Costs & Aid page. The Wharton Youth Network membership is included.

wharton-future-of-the-business-world-onl.about:
Future of the Business World is an intensive online programme from Wharton Global Youth for students around the world. Each weekday includes two hours of live lectures and one hour of TA-led recitation, plus simulations, small-group work and independent study; students choose a morning (08:00–11:00 EDT) or afternoon (13:00–16:00 EDT) block. Topics include design thinking, scenario planning, market research and business communication, and teams finish with a project predicting future business trends.

2027 sessions run 14–25 June and 5–16 July. The programme is for students currently in grades 9–12; the priority deadline is 27 January 2027, after which admission is rolling. Completers receive a Wharton Global Youth Certificate of Completion.
highlights: Live Wharton lectures with two time blocks for different time zones
Two business simulations and a team project
Certificate of completion
wharton-future-of-the-business-world-onl.eligibility: Students currently in grades 9–12 from anywhere in the world with good English.
how_to_apply: Check the 2027 session dates and time block on the programme page
Submit the Wharton Global Youth online application (opens November 2026)
Apply by the 27 January 2027 priority deadline (later applications are considered while places remain)
Pay tuition once admitted and test your internet connection and time zone
wharton-future-of-the-business-world-onl.costs: Paid online programme; fees on Wharton Global Youth's Costs & Aid page. The Wharton Youth Network membership is included.

wharton-leadership-in-the-business-world.about:
Leadership in the Business World (LBW) is a selective residential summer programme run by the Wharton School's Global Youth Program. Students attend lectures by Wharton faculty, visit companies, hear from business leaders and work in teams on a business plan that they pitch to a panel of judges at the end of the session.

The 2027 programme runs in three three-week sessions (6–26 June, 27 June–17 July, 18 July–7 August 2027) in Philadelphia, with around 120 students selected per session. It is designed for students currently in grade 11 with demonstrated leadership experience and an unweighted GPA of at least 3.5; international applicants are explicitly welcome.

The 2027 fee is USD 12,299 (plus a USD 100 application fee). Admissions are need-blind, but fee waivers and most scholarships are restricted to specific groups (Philadelphia students, partner nominees, Caribbean access), so most international students should expect to pay in full.
highlights: Taught by Wharton faculty on the Penn campus
Team business-plan competition judged by industry professionals
International applicants welcome; about 120 places per session
wharton-leadership-in-the-business-world.eligibility: Students currently in grade 11 (rising seniors) with demonstrated leadership experience and an unweighted GPA of at least 3.5. Open to students of any nationality; English proficiency is required.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 programme page and check your grade fits
Create an account and submit the Wharton Global Youth online application (opens November 2026)
Upload transcript, short essays and a recommendation as requested; pay the USD 100 application fee
Apply by the priority deadline (27 January 2027) for the best chance of a place and of scholarship review
If admitted, confirm your place and arrange a US visa if you are not American
wharton-leadership-in-the-business-world.costs: 2027 fee USD 12,299 (tuition, housing, most meals) plus USD 100 non-refundable application fee; travel and visa extra. Limited need-based scholarships for specific groups (Philadelphia public schools, partner nominees, Caribbean residents); fee waivers are not available to international applicants.

wharton-management-technology-summer-ins.about:
The Management & Technology Summer Institute (M&TSI) is run by Penn's Jerome Fisher Program in Management & Technology, a joint programme of the Wharton School and Penn Engineering. Over three weeks students take classes from Penn faculty in engineering and management, visit companies, and work in teams to build a technology prototype and a go-to-market plan that they pitch at the end.

The 2027 institute runs 11–31 July in Philadelphia for rising high-school seniors. Selection is based on academic achievement and extracurricular leadership; successful participants earn one college credit unit from Penn Engineering. Applications open 2 November 2026 and close 27 January 2027, with decisions from 24 March.

The 2027 on-campus fee is USD 11,999 plus a USD 100 application fee. Need-based scholarships (full or partial) are available to a limited number of applicants through a separate financial-aid form. The page does not state international eligibility, so international students should confirm before applying.
highlights: Earn one Penn Engineering college credit
Build and pitch a tech prototype with a go-to-market plan
Need-based full and partial scholarships available
wharton-management-technology-summer-ins.eligibility: Rising high-school seniors (current grade 11) with strong academics and leadership. International eligibility is not stated on the page; confirm with the programme office.
how_to_apply: Read the M&TSI 2027 page and check eligibility
Submit the online application between 2 November 2026 and 27 January 2027
Submit the separate financial-aid form if you need a scholarship
Wait for decisions from 24 March 2027 (some rolling decisions follow)
wharton-management-technology-summer-ins.costs: 2027 fee USD 11,999 plus USD 100 application fee; travel, off-campus meals and medical costs extra. Need-based full or partial scholarships for a limited number of students.

wharton-moneyball-academy-2027.about:
Moneyball Academy is a three-week residential summer programme run with Wharton Sports Analytics. Students learn statistics, data analysis and programming tools used by professional sports teams, analyse real sports data, hear from analysts and executives in the sports industry, and present a final research project.

The 2027 session runs 27 June–17 July in Philadelphia for students currently in grades 10–11 (rising juniors and seniors). International applicants are welcome. The 2027 fee is USD 10,999 plus a USD 100 application fee.
highlights: Real sports data and Wharton Sports Analytics faculty
Builds statistics and data-science skills
International applicants welcome
wharton-moneyball-academy-2027.eligibility: Students currently in grades 10–11 of any nationality with strong maths and good English.

wharton-moneyball-training-camp-online-2.about:
Moneyball: Training Camp is a one-week online programme that introduces statistics through a sports lens. Taught by Wharton Professor Adi Wyner, it covers statistics fundamentals, regression and probability with hands-on programming in R, and each student builds their own sports-analysis project and earns a Wharton Global Youth certificate.

2027 sessions: 21–25 June and 19–23 July. Open to students currently in grades 9–12; international applicants are welcome. Priority deadline 27 January 2027, then rolling admission.
highlights: Taught by Wharton statistics professor Adi Wyner
Learn R programming on real sports data
Short one-week format

wharton-product-design-academy-2027.about:
Product Design Academy is a hands-on, three-week residential programme that teaches design thinking from user research to working prototype. Students work in teams to identify a real problem, generate ideas and build prototypes using Penn's Studios@Venture Labs, then learn how to turn a product into a business and present a final showcase.

The 2027 session runs 6–26 June in Philadelphia for students currently in grades 10–11. No business background is required and international applicants are welcome. The 2027 fee is USD 10,999 plus a USD 100 application fee.
highlights: Prototype in Penn's Venture Labs studios
Design thinking plus business planning
No prior business experience needed
wharton-product-design-academy-2027.eligibility: Students currently in grades 10–11 of any nationality with good English.

wharton-sports-business-academy-online-2.about:
Sports Business Academy is a selective three-week online programme sponsored by the Wharton Sports Analytics and Business Initiative. Through faculty lectures, case discussions and guest speakers, students study how sports leagues, media rights, marketing, labour relations and social responsibility work, and complete a capstone analysing an emerging professional league.

In 2026 it ran 5–24 July with live sessions roughly 10:00–15:30 EDT; 2027 dates are not yet posted but the 2027 priority deadline is 27 January and the final deadline 17 March 2027. The page lists eligibility as students currently in grades 10–11 (rising juniors and seniors); international applicants are welcome.

Guest speakers from the sports industry
Capstone project on a professional league

who-europe-summer-school-ncd-2027.about:
The WHO Regional Office for Europe, its Collaborating Centre at Université Côte d'Azur and the Ulysseus European University run an annual summer school on systems thinking and innovation for the prevention of noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) and healthy ageing. The 2027 edition takes place in Nice, France, on 20–23 July 2027 (09:00–14:00 daily), in English.

The curriculum is expected to cover systems-thinking methods, archetypes and policy scenarios, decision-making tools, designing systems-informed studies, policy innovation, AI for public health and innovation ecosystems.

There is no tuition fee; lunch, coffee breaks and a welcome dinner are included. Only 30 in-person places: apply by 23 November 2026.
highlights: Run by WHO/Europe
No tuition fee; meals included
Only 30 participants
who-europe-summer-school-ncd-2027.eligibility: PhD students and early- and mid-career professionals (researchers, postgraduates, health practitioners, policy-makers). Selection on experience, education, personal statement and collaboration potential.
how_to_apply: Read the WHO/Europe call.
Prepare a personal statement and CV.
Submit the online WHO form by 23 November 2026.
Wait for notification by 18 December 2026.
who-europe-summer-school-ncd-2027.costs: Free tuition; lunches, coffee breaks and a welcome dinner included. Participants pay travel and accommodation.

whu-bachelor-european-summer-program-202.about:
WHU's Bachelor European Summer Program (BESP) runs 23 May – 11 June 2027 on the Vallendar campus near Koblenz, Germany. It has ten academic modules taught in English, including trade integration in Europe, European capital markets, family firms, German history, sustainability, entrepreneurship, European marketing and business tax.

Company and financial-institution visits plus a cultural programme complement 65 academic hours (listed as 10–14 ECTS / 5–7 US credits). Frankfurt airport pick-up is included.

It is for bachelor students nominated by WHU partner schools (tuition is generally waived for nominated students). Apply before 31 March 2027.
highlights: Top German business school
Company and bank visits
Tuition generally waived for partner nominees
whu-bachelor-european-summer-program-202.eligibility: Bachelor students nominated by a WHU partner university (check WHU's Global Partner Network).

Ask your international office to nominate you.
Register on the WHU registration-and-fee page before 31 March 2027.
Pay the base fee by 15 April 2027.
whu-bachelor-european-summer-program-202.costs: Base fee on the WHU registration-and-fee page (non-refundable); tuition generally waived for partner-nominated students.

world-scholars-cup-accra-round-2027.about:
The World Scholar's Cup (WSC) is an international academic tournament for school students that rewards curiosity rather than memorisation. Teams of three prepare an interdisciplinary annual theme spanning science, history, art, music and literature, then compete in four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (individual multiple-choice test) and the Scholar's Bowl (team quiz). Rounds also include social events such as a talent show and Scholar's Ball.

The Accra round takes place on 13–14 February 2027 at Brainy Bairn School. Students can take part through a school club or independently with at least two teammates; regional rounds are open to students from any country, and good results qualify teams for the next Global Round and, from there, the Tournament of Champions at Yale University.
highlights: Four team events: debate, writing, quiz bowl and challenge test
Open to independent teams as well as school clubs
Qualifies strong teams for the Global Round and Yale Tournament of Champions
world-scholars-cup-accra-round-2027.eligibility: School students (typically ages 10–18) in teams of three, from any school or country; students may enter independently without a school club.
how_to_apply: Form a team of three (school club or independent)
Sign up on the World Scholar's Cup site and indicate your intent to attend this round
Register the team online by the deadline on the Calendar & Registration page
Study the 2026–27 theme and curriculum (most teams prepare 2–8 weeks)
Attend the round in Accra on 13–14 February 2027
world-scholars-cup-accra-round-2027.costs: Registration fee per student set by WSC for each round (not shown on the calendar page); travel and accommodation extra.

world-scholars-cup-chisinau-round-2027.about:
The World Scholar's Cup is an international academic tournament for school students in teams of three. Every round covers the same interdisciplinary annual theme and has four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (an individual multiple-choice test) and the Scholar's Bowl (a team quiz), plus a talent show and social events.

Regional rounds are open to any team that registers, wherever its members live, so students can travel to a nearby round. Junior (roughly ages 10-14) and Senior (roughly 14-18) divisions compete separately, and strong results at a regional round earn an invitation to a Global Round and then the Tournament of Champions at Yale.

The Chișinău Round runs on 26-27 March 2027 at Heritage International School in Moldova's capital.
highlights: Regional round in Chișinău on 26-27 March 2027
Debate, writing, quiz and individual challenge in English
Pathway to Global Rounds
world-scholars-cup-chisinau-round-2027.eligibility: School students in the Junior or Senior division, registering as teams of three (individuals can usually be placed in a team). Any nationality may register for any regional round. All events are in English.
how_to_apply: Open the round page on scholarscup.org and check the dates and host school.
Form a team of three (or ask to be matched) with an adult coach or parent contact.
Complete the round's registration form or request info from the organisers.
Pay the round fee and study the season theme and curriculum.
Travel to the host city for the two-day round.
world-scholars-cup-chisinau-round-2027.costs: Paid: each round charges a per-student registration fee set on its registration form; travel, accommodation and meals are paid by participants.

wu-vienna-international-summer-universit.about:
The International Summer University (ISU) at WU Vienna, one of Europe's largest business universities, runs 28 June – 16 July 2027. Students take two intensive, practice-oriented courses back to back (1.5 weeks each, 4 ECTS each) on business, economics and management topics, alongside a social and cultural programme in Vienna.

It is open to undergraduate and graduate students from WU partner universities worldwide (check whether your university is a partner).

Applications run 15 February – 31 March 2027; partner universities nominate by 15 March.
highlights: 8 ECTS in three weeks
Practice-oriented business courses
Social programme in Vienna
wu-vienna-international-summer-universit.eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate students from WU partner universities worldwide.
how_to_apply: Check if your university is a WU partner.
Ask your international office for a nomination by 15 March 2027.
Apply online between 15 February and 31 March 2027.
Pay fees as listed on WU's fees page.
wu-vienna-international-summer-universit.costs: Fees on the WU 'Fees, Services and Payment' page.

yonsei-winter-abroad-2026-27.about:
Winter Abroad at Yonsei (WAY) is a three-week, credit-bearing winter study-abroad programme taught in English at Yonsei University's Sinchon campus in central Seoul. Classes run 22 December 2026 – 8 January 2027, with optional orientation, campus dormitories (SK Global House, International House, Woo Jung Won) and a closing commencement ceremony; students can take one to three 3-credit courses.

It is open to undergraduate, master's and doctoral students at universities outside Korea and to high-school seniors with an official university admission letter, subject to a minimum GPA and a comprehensive review. The general application deadline is 12 November 2026, so apply quickly; small scholarships (for example a KRW 200,000 alumni scholarship) must be requested within the application period.

yunus-emre-thematic-summer-schools-2027.about:
Every year the Yunus Emre Institute organises international Thematic Summer Schools in different Turkish cities. Recent themes are archaeology (with site visits and digs), contemporary Turkish art, Turkish cuisine and Turkish fashion. Each programme combines on-site training, workshops and visits with Turkish practice.

They suit university students and young adults interested in culture, heritage, gastronomy or design who want a short, guided stay in Türkiye. Calls are published on the institute's site and through its centres abroad (including Tbilisi).

yunus-emre-turkish-summer-school-2027.about:
Türkçe Yaz Okulu (Turkish Summer School) is the Yunus Emre Institute's flagship summer programme. It brings together people learning Turkish as a foreign language at levels A1 to C2 for intensive courses run with universities across Türkiye, following a standard curriculum that balances all language skills and moves learning out of the classroom into daily life.

The language programme is combined with excursions, museum and heritage-site visits, workshops and cultural events. Participants are drawn from students of the institute's Turkish courses at its centres abroad (including Tbilisi, Baku and other cities) or its online courses. It is one of the most affordable ways to spend a summer in Türkiye while gaining a recognised language certificate.

yunus-emre-turkology-summer-school-2027.about:
Alongside its Turkish Summer School, the Yunus Emre Institute runs a Turkology Summer School for undergraduate and graduate students of Turkology (Turkish language and literature) departments at universities outside Türkiye. Participants need at least B1 Turkish.

The curriculum covers the structure, history and vocabulary of Turkish, text analysis and literary history, taught by specialist academics, and is combined with trips and cultural programmes across Türkiye. Students of Turkology at Georgian, Azerbaijani, Central Asian or other universities can use it to deepen their academic Turkish and build contacts with Turkish universities.
